name: swiss-editorial
title: Swiss Editorial
description: High-contrast editorial typography on warm paper, with exposed twelve-column grids, crisp rules, and a disciplined signal-red accent.

typography.fontFamily: Source Serif 4, Georgia, Times New Roman, serif
typography.monospaceFamily: IBM Plex Mono, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace
typography.displayFamily: Source Serif 4, Georgia, Times New Roman, serif

rules: Lead with editorial hierarchy: display serif for narrative and grotesk or mono for controls and metadata.
Expose the twelve-column grid through aligned rules rather than decorative containers.
Keep article measure between 58ch and 72ch; captions may be narrower but never full viewport width.
Use warm paper, ink, and one signal-red action color; do not add gradient illustration.
Separate stories with 1px rules and generous white space instead of floating every section in a card.
Set display lines at 0.95–1.05 and body copy at 1.55–1.7.
Use asymmetric spans such as 7/5 or 8/4 to avoid generic centered hero compositions.
Align folios, timestamps, and numeric indexes with tabular figures.
Keep corners nearly square; rounding must never soften the editorial grid.
Motion is limited to restrained underline, reveal, and selection feedback within 180ms.
